[reuse-established-capabilities] Retention decisions derive from Tenant Config Service's `audit_retention_days` and its existing change history; physical cleanup uses atomic partition deletion via the nightly maintenance framework without becoming the unreadability boundary.

[provability] Compliance can prove the effective retention period on any past date by reading Tenant Config's setting history (or an equivalent owner-held record), without Audit Service becoming a second authority for the setting.

[open-and-closed-decisions-named] The artifact explicitly names which decisions it deliberately leaves open for a possible future multi-region deployment (e.g., where the retention authority would live per region) and which it closes now, each with a one-line reason, without proposing phases, roadmap or timelines.
[no-roadmap] There is no 'phase 2', 'future work' roadmap, or compatibility path for the uncommitted multi-region case.

[failure-semantics] A failed or late nightly deletion remains observable and retryable but cannot make an expired partition readable; a setting change takes effect only at its next UTC day boundary and is resolved from Tenant Config history.
